name: Instinct
tagline: Treatment-sheet-first clinical records and hospital workflow software for veterinary practices.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is vertical clinical software sold to animal hospitals, not a tool one person uses at a desk, so the whole premise of a personal replacement is shaky before you write a line of code. The name is shared by several unrelated products, so confirm you are looking at the veterinary one before trusting any detail here. What an agent can build in a weekend is the visible part: patients, orders, a time-slot treatment grid, checkboxes with timestamps. What it cannot build is the part hospitals actually buy: a drug formulary someone else maintains, lab and practice-management integrations, controlled substance audit trails, and real-time state shared across a shift change at 3am. If you are a solo practitioner or a very stubborn pet owner tracking meds for one animal, the consolation build below is genuinely fine.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you enter a patient, add recurring treatment orders, and tick off a 24 hour time-slot grid with timestamps and initials, then print a shift handoff sheet.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine you leave on
Willingness to hand-enter your own drug list and doses
Nobody else needing to see the same screen at the same time
whatYouLose: Real-time shared treatment sheets across multiple people and shifts, which is the actual product
A maintained drug formulary with dosing and safety checks, instead of a JSON file you typed yourself
Lab, imaging, and practice-management integrations that stop double entry
Controlled substance logs and audit trails that survive an inspection
Tablet and phone clients, plus someone to call when it breaks mid-shift
moatNotes: Clinical software gets replaced roughly never, because migration happens while the hospital is still running.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the software is load-bearing during hours when a mistake is measured in an animal, not a support ticket. A hospital pays for shared live state, a formulary maintained by someone else, integrations that kill duplicate data entry, records that hold up under review, and a vendor on the hook when a server dies. None of that is a feature list you can clone; it is an operational commitment with a phone number attached.
notes: The treatment grid is a weekend; the trust is not. The moat is shared live clinical state, a maintained formulary, and the fact that nobody swaps their records system while the hospital is open.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user veterinary treatment sheet tracker. It runs on my machine, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite through better-sqlite3, data file at ./data/app.db. Start with npm run dev on localhost. No auth, no external APIs, so no .env is needed; if you later add anything requiring a key, read it from .env and commit a .env.example instead.

Data model: Patient (name, species, breed, weight in kg, owner name, notes). Stay (patient, admit time, discharge time nullable, presenting problem). Order (stay, label, category from med / fluid / monitoring / nursing, dose text, route, frequency in hours, start time, end time nullable). Task (order, scheduled time, status from pending / done / skipped, done time, initials, note).

Core behavior:
- Creating or editing an Order regenerates its Tasks from start time to end time at the given frequency, preserving any Task already marked done or skipped.
- The stay page shows a treatment grid: rows are Orders, columns are hourly slots for a chosen 24 hour window, cells are the Tasks. Clicking a cell cycles pending to done to skipped, stamps the real clock time, and prompts once for initials which it remembers in localStorage.
- Overdue pending Tasks (scheduled time more than 30 minutes in the past) render red. Due within the hour renders amber.
- A weight-based dose helper: pick a drug from ./data/drugs.json (seed it with about ten entries, each with name, mg per kg range, route, and a warning string), enter patient weight, see the computed range. It is a calculator, not advice, and it says so on screen.
- A printable handoff view per stay: patient summary, active orders, everything done in the last 12 hours with times and initials, everything overdue. Plain print stylesheet, no dialogs.
- CSV export of Tasks for a stay.

Explicitly out of scope: billing, inventory, invoicing, lab or imaging integrations, multi-user or realtime sync, controlled substance compliance logging, mobile app, any hosted deployment.

Deliver: the app, a seed script that creates two demo patients with active stays, and a README covering how to run it, where the database lives, how to back it up, and a short paragraph saying this is a personal tracker and not a clinical system of record.
